paper.title: Deciphering spatial domains from spatially resolved transcriptomics with an adaptive graph attention auto-encoder

eligibility: Development reading preceded these tests; not a held-out paper. Own diagrams/controls/repairs do not add original cases.
question: How do spatial support, expression features, optional preclustering, learned attention and reconstruction connect without conflating spatial adjacency with directed aggregation?

elements_and_relations.visible: Left construction stage connects physical spot positions to a spatial neighbour graph; the optional cell-type-aware construction is grouped by a dashed blue box.
elements_and_relations.meaning: Radius support is undirected; expression-derived prelabels prune cross-label edges in the optional branch, retaining spots. Prelabels are not verified cell types.
elements_and_relations.evidence: Figure1/caption and Methods Construction of SNN/cell type-aware SNN; source-review S01/S02

elements_and_relations.visible: Central encoder/decoder links input gene expression, embedding and reconstructed expression; attention operates on graph neighbours.
elements_and_relations.meaning: Fixed TensorFlow forward distinguishes shared M, two attention parameter sets, mixed T, transposed weights and reused T. These details rely on code/methods rather than icon appearance alone.
elements_and_relations.evidence: Methods Eq1–7; fixed model.py encoder/decoder; S03/S04

elements_and_relations.visible: Right side groups applications including domains, denoising and 3D.
elements_and_relations.meaning: Downstream domain clustering is different from preclustering. 3D needs aligned slices and cross-slice graph support. The new drawing is explicitly single-slice.
